clue.text: Skirt around first of bollards in taxi

parts.note: a mini is a very short skirt
ca, short for circa, means around or about a date

indicators.note: first of asks for only the opening letter of the word bollards

explanation.surface: A taxi driver steers round the front bollard to get through.
explanation.definitionFit: A minicab is a hired car working like a taxi, booked by phone rather than hailed.

clue.text: Feral horse gets little Stanley in the face

indicators.note: in means the short name is placed inside the slang word for face

parts.note: mug is slang for face
Stan is a short form of the name Stanley

explanation.surface: A wild horse kicks a man called Stan in the face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feral' could tempt you towards an anagram, but it simply belongs to the definition; the container signal is 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mustang is a free-roaming wild horse of the American West, descended from domestic stock.

clue.text: Is any murder criminal, nanny?

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters of is any murder are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking a children's nanny whether every murder is a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges ISANYMURDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursemaid or nursery maid looks after young children, the job of a nanny.

clue.text: Doctor wearing outer garment, sort of jacket

indicators.note: wearing means having something on, so the doctor goes inside the garment

parts.note: a coat is worn over other clothes
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A doctor in an overcoat, wearing some kind of jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: A combat jacket is a camouflage military jacket; 'wearing' signals the container, with the coat on the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A combat jacket is a military-style jacket, so the word works as a modifier naming a kind of jacket.

clue.text: Dogs chasing widely-spread sheep

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so this piece comes second

parts.note: broad means wide, spread out
to dog someone is to tail them, follow closely

explanation.surface: Dogs chase sheep that have scattered over the hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dogs' is a verb here, meaning follows; 'chasing' puts it second.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadtail is a karakul lamb or its flat glossy fleece, so the plural names such sheep.

clue.text: Hearty, sat out in front of a Parisian church

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the three letters of sat are rearranged

parts.note: un is French for a, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: Someone sits out in the open before a Paris church, feeling hale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' signals the anagram; 'in front of' is a link, the pieces simply running in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Staunch support and hearty support are both wholehearted and loyal, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Nothing in mostly dull game

indicators.note: in means the zero goes inside the shortened word
mostly means all but the last letter of the word is kept

parts.note: slow can mean dull or uninteresting
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing happens in a largely boring game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts SLOW to SLO; 'in' puts O inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Solo, or solo whist, is a card game in which one player may play against the others.

clue.text: Heavenly, a cake decoration

parts.note: angelic means like an angel, heavenly

explanation.surface: A cake decoration described as divine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavenly' reads as praise of the cake but is ANGELIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Candied stalks of the angelica plant are cut into green strips to decorate cakes.

clue.text: The head, eccentric type

definitions.meaning: slang for the head, as in use your noggin
slang for a crazy or obsessive person, a crank

explanation.definitionFit: Nut is slang both for the head and for a madcap person, a crank.

clue.text: Short durable cape that's the gear

indicators.note: short means the word is cut by its last letter

parts.note: hard means tough, durable
a ness is a headland or cape, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Dungeness

explanation.surface: A tough short cape forms part of a horse's tack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts HARD to HAR; 'that's the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A harness is the set of straps and fittings, the gear, by which a horse is attached to a cart.

clue.text: Knight is backing king

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word is is read from right to left

parts.note: R, from Latin rex, is the usual abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A knight shows loyalty to his monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses only the little word 'is', not the king.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight is addressed by the title Sir, so the honorific stands for the knighted man.

clue.text: One holding another job, doctor on barge

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
taken as written
a lighter is a flat-bottomed barge used for unloading ships

explanation.surface: A doctor working a second shift on a canal barge.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who moonlights takes a second job on the side, often at night and undeclared.

clue.text: Positioned in a river in Australian city

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the run made by a and the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
laid means put in position, placed

explanation.surface: Something placed in a river beside an Australian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container; the Dee splits around the placed word, leaving the A at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Adelaide is the capital of South Australia, a state capital city on the Torrens.

clue.text: Satisfy publican at first with tenancy agreement

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the word publican

parts.note: a lease is a contract granting tenancy of property

explanation.surface: A pub landlord is keen to sign a new tenancy deal with the brewery.
explanation.definitionFit: To please someone is to satisfy or gratify them, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Play with plaything

definitions.meaning: Ibsen's 1879 drama about Nora Helmer has this title
a miniature house for dolls is a child's toy

explanation.definitionFit: Ibsen wrote a famous play of this name, and the phrase is also a toy home for dolls.

clue.text: Devastated city to be rebuilt, Owen learns

indicators.note: to be rebuilt means the letters of owen learns are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A man named Owen discovers a ruined city is to be reconstructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be rebuilt' rearranges OWENLEARNS; the city was devastated by Hurricane Katrina in 2005.
explanation.definitionFit: New Orleans was devastated by Hurricane Katrina in 2005, so the city fits the description.

clue.text: But it also treats women

parts.note: read as a London hospital whose name sounds as if it cares only for men, which in fact sees patients of both sexes

explanation.surface: A remark that some clinic, despite its name, takes female patients too.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy's Hospital is a famous London teaching hospital; its name, read as plain English, means 'men', hence 'But ... also women'.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural noun for men or fellows doubles as the name of the London hospital founded by Thomas Guy.

clue.text: Found, ornate mace and a crucifix

indicators.note: ornate means elaborately worked, so the letters of mace and a are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
a crucifix is a cross bearing the figure of Christ

explanation.surface: Treasure hunters turn up a decorated ceremonial mace and a crucifix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ornate' rearranges MACE and A into CAMEA; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To come across something is to find it by chance, a phrasal-verb synonym of found.

clue.text: More than happy, former lover not moving, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the words are as heard, so the spoken phrase gives the spelling

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled that an old flame has stopped coming round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' means EX + STATIC said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstatic means overwhelmed with joy, so it is more than merely happy.

clue.text: University head's in luck, getting cycle back

parts.note: chance means luck or fortune

indicators.note: back means the word for a cycle is turned round to read the other way

parts.note: a roll is a turning over, a revolution or cycle

explanation.surface: A vice-chancellor has the good fortune to get a stolen bicycle returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' signals the reversal; 'getting' is a link and the 's after head is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: In British universities the chancellor is the titular head, with day-to-day running left to a vice-chancellor.

clue.text: Joke about famous apple

indicators.note: about means one word goes round the other

parts.note: cod, as a verb, means to joke or hoax
star means famous, as in a star player

explanation.surface: A joke told about a famous apple.
explanation.walkthrough: Cod as a verb (to hoax) is British informal usage; 'about' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Costard is an old English variety of large cooking apple, the root of costermonger.

clue.text: Young person nicking pound in nightspot

indicators.note: nicking, in the sense of stealing, here means taking a piece into the middle of another

parts.note: a cub is a young person, as in a cub reporter, or a junior Scout
L, from Latin libra, abbreviates the pound sterling

explanation.surface: A youngster is caught stealing money at a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nicking' (British slang for stealing) puts L inside CUB.
explanation.definitionFit: A club is a venue for late-night dancing and drinking, the standard sense of nightspot.

clue.text: Small caterpillar climbing over one rotten sprout

indicators.note: climbing, in a down clue, means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a grub is a small larva, like a young caterpillar

indicators.note: rotten means gone bad, so the letters of one are disordered

explanation.surface: A tiny caterpillar crawls up over a rotten shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns GRUB into BURG; 'rotten' rearranges ONE into EON; 'over' places one above the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To burgeon is to put out buds or shoots, so it means to sprout.

clue.text: A blow for one of rowing crew

definitions.meaning: a hit with a hand or weapon
the oarsman nearest the stern who sets the rhythm

explanation.definitionFit: A stroke is a blow, and also the oarsman who sets the pace in a rowing eight.

clue.text: Not very exciting appointment in Kent?

parts.note: Kent is a county in South-East England, abbreviated SE
a date is an appointment to meet someone

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a planned meeting in Kent will be a dull affair.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in South-East England, so an appointment there is a DATE in SE, written SE + DATE; the question mark flags this loose 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedate means calm, unhurried and staid, so something sedate is not very exciting.

clue.text: Christian, perhaps, a quarrel-maker?

definitions.meaning: ... Christian led the mutiny on the Bounty, so Christian is an example of a man with this first name
a quarrel is a square-headed crossbow bolt, and the craftsman who made arrows and bolts bore this trade name

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a Christian might be someone who stirs up arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christian' suggests a churchgoer and 'quarrel' a row, but one is the Bounty mutineer's surname and the other a crossbow bolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A fletcher was an arrow-maker, and Fletcher Christian was the Bounty mutineer.

clue.text: Singer in musical (Tommy)

indicators.note: in means the answer sits inside the words musical and Tommy

explanation.surface: A singer appears in the rock musical Tommy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to letters inside musicAL TOmmy.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice.

clue.text: Drink — all do it wildly after a short working day

indicators.note: after places the scrambled letters behind the a and the short day

parts.note: taken as written
Mon is the short form of Monday, a working day

indicators.note: wildly means the letters of all do it are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Everybody drinks with abandon once a brief Monday shift is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' gives TILLADO, which 'after' puts behind the A and the abbreviated Monday.
explanation.definitionFit: Amontillado is a medium-dry sherry, so it is a kind of drink.

clue.text: Aristocrat wasting time away

indicators.note: wasting means losing or using up, so one letter is dropped from the word for an aristocrat

parts.note: toff is British slang for an upper-class person

explanation.surface: A nobleman squanders his hours while he is away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasting' drops T from TOFF.
explanation.definitionFit: Off means away, as in going off on holiday or a day off.

clue.text: Operate combine without starter key

indicators.note: without starter means the opening letter is dropped, here when that letter is the key

parts.note: to fuse is to combine or blend together
F is a musical key

explanation.surface: Instructions to run a combine harvester without the ignition key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combine' looks like a farm machine but means FUSE; dropping its first letter, the musical key F, leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To use a machine is to operate it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Fed cat —- nothing cooked, actually

indicators.note: cooked means falsified or messed about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: The cat was fed, but nothing was actually cooked for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges FEDCAT plus O into the Latin phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means in fact or in reality, as opposed to by right, so it matches actually.

clue.text: Spotted entertaining ambassador and bishop in unlicensed premises

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so one word holds the others inside

parts.note: seen means spotted or noticed
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: An ambassador and a bishop are seen drinking in an illegal bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' signals the container: 'Spotted' is the host, holding the ambassador's title and bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebeen, originally Irish, is an unlicensed drinking den selling illicit alcohol.
